items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names follow the package's style (`encode(e *encoder)`, `decode(d *decoder)`, `nvertices`, `loopSizes`, `totalVerts`). Exported Encode/Decode methods have doc comments. Short names like d/e/v are the codebase's own idiom.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Encode/Decode went into the already-large shapeindex.go instead of the requested shapeindex_encode.go. The 'make cap min(n,1024); for range; readFloat64 x3; append' loop is copy-pasted across lax_loop, lax_polyline, point_vector, loop, and polygon. It also includes unrelated fixes (ChainEdge, ChainPosition, applyUpdatesInternal).

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Every length is bounded before allocating (`nvertices > maxEncodedVertices`, a running totalVerts check, capped capacities). It checks d.err after each read, adds face-run count validation and a CRC32 trailer, and validates shape and edge IDs. Tests cover every truncated prefix and every corrupted byte.

items.name: Existing encodings and Shape interface unchanged
items.name_zh: 既有编码格式与 Shape 接口不变
items.evidence: Changes are additive: Loop and LaxLoop get typeTagLoop/typeTagLaxLoop, and the per-shape wire formats are unchanged. However, the diff also changes existing shape behavior: LaxLoop.ChainEdge (`j+1 != l.numVertices`), LaxPolygon.ChainPosition, PointVector.ChainEdge, plus a genericShape addition in shape.go.
